'''Rebecca Walo Omana''' (born 15 July 1951)<!--full dates in infobox, per MOS--> is a Congolese [[mathematician]], [[professor]], and [[Religious sister (Catholic)|reverend sister]]. Omana became the first female mathematics professor in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] in 1982.<ref name = "awma profile"> {{Cite web| title = Rebecca Walo OMANA| work = African Women in Mathematics Association| accessdate = 2021-01-15| url = http://africanwomeninmath.org/women-in-math/portrait/rebecca-walo-omana}} </ref> She is the director of the mathematics and informatics doctoral program at the [[University of Kinshasa]] and is a vice-president of the [[African Women in Mathematics Association]].<ref name = "diocese"> {{Cite web| last = OKONDJO| first = Pierre Claude| title = LE PROFIL DU RECTEUR DE L'UNIVERSITÉ NOTRE-DAME DE TSHUMBE| work = DIOCÈSE DE TSHUMBE| accessdate = 2021-01-16| url = http://anjaashiwatshumbe.over-blog.org/2018/01/le-profil-du-nouveau-recteur-de-l-universite-notre-dame-de-tshumbe.html}} </ref> Her mathematical interests lie in [[differential equations]], [[nonlinear analysis]], and modeling.

== Biography ==
Omana was born in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], on 15 July 1951. She was passionate about mathematics during high school.<ref name = "awma profile"/> She made her religious profession to the [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] Soeurs de St Francois d'Assise at the age of 18, and made her sacred vows in 1978.<ref> {{Cite web| last = Marie| first = diocese-tshumbe-ste| title = SOEURS DE ST FRANCOIS D´ASSISE| work = Diocèse de Tshumbe Sainte Marie| accessdate = 2021-01-18| url = http://diocese-tshumbe-ste-marie.over-blog.com/pages/SOEURS_DE_ST_FRANCOIS_DASSISE-6871492.html}} </ref><ref name = "diocese"/>

Omana earned a bachelor’s of science in mathematics from the [[Université du Québec à Montréal]] in 1979. She earned her master’s of science in 1982 from the [[Université Laval]]. In both institutions, she was the only African woman in the department.<ref name = "awma profile"/> Of this period Omana says:

<blockquote>
I had to double effort to be better and remove negative prejudices in the heads of my colleagues and my professors to be accepted. But in view of results, I was not only accepted but invited by groups of colleagues for research works. <ref name = "awma profile"/>
</blockquote>

In 1982, Omana began working as a lecturer and became the first female mathematics professor in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]].<ref name="awma profile" />

Omana earned her [[Master of Advanced Studies#France and francophone countries|Diplôme d'études approfondies]] in 1985 and her Ph.D. in 1990 from the [[Université catholique de Louvain]] where she worked with advisor [[Jean Mawhin]].<ref name="awma profile" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Rébecca Walo Omana - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=100656|access-date=2022-02-11|website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> She was the first Congolese woman to earn a doctorate there.<ref name="diocese" />

At the founding of the quarterly multidisciplinary journal ''la revue Notre Dame de la Sagesse'' (RENODAS), Omana was listed as the director.<ref>{{Cite web| title = La Revue Notre-Dame de la Sagesse| work = UNIVERSITÉ NOTRE-DAME DE TSHUMBE| accessdate = 2021-01-16| url = https://www.unitshu.ac.cd/renodas.html| archive-date = 2021-01-22| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210122031402/https://www.unitshu.ac.cd/renodas.html| url-status = dead}}</ref> She has supervised numerous doctoral students.<ref name=":0" /> She hopes that some of her doctoral students will join her among the small number of female professors in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.<ref name="awma profile" /> Omana heads the mathematics doctoral program at the University of Kinshasa.<ref name="awma profile" /> Since 2010,<ref name="diocese" /> she has served as the rector for the Université Notre-Dame de Tshumbe (UNITSHU), a Catholic public university which was founded in 2010 in [[Tshumbe]], Democratic Republic of the Congo.<ref>{{Cite web| title = Présentation de l'Université Notre Dame de Tshumbe| work = UNIVERSITÉ NOTRE-DAME DE TSHUMBE| accessdate = 2021-01-18| url = https://www.unitshu.ac.cd/Presentation.html| archive-date = 2021-01-22| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210122184523/https://www.unitshu.ac.cd/Presentation.html| url-status = dead}}</ref>

== Mathematical works ==
{{expand section|date=January 2021}}
Omana has published two mathematics books<ref name = "diocese" /> and over 20 mathematics articles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2025 |title=Rebecca Walo Omana |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rebecca-Walo-Omana |access-date=May 27, 2025 |website=ResearchGate}}</ref> Her work on ordinary differential equations and [[fuzzy logic]] has had applications in fields such as epidemiology and law. Her mathematics articles are mostly centered on mathematical modelling and functional analysis.

== Personal life ==

Omana's parents are not academics, but some siblings hold master's degrees.<ref name="awma profile" /> Her teachers and father influenced her decision to become a mathematician.<ref name="awma profile" />

She has said "mathematics is fantastic; as its name is female, it is a domain that should belong to us women".<ref name = "awma profile"/>{{efn|Referring to the French word ''mathématiques'', which has the [[French grammar#Gender|feminine gender]]}}

== Academic leadership ==

Omana has served as Director of the doctoral programme in Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Kinshasa, where she has supervised doctoral research and contributed to the development of postgraduate mathematics education. Since 2010, she has also served as Rector of the Université Notre-Dame de Tshumbe, a Catholic university in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=WALO OMANA REBECCA
 |url=https://www.unikin.ac.cd/oipr/OIPR/chercheurs/963/WALO-OMANA-REBECCA
 |website=University of Kinshasa
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Research ==

Omana's research focuses on nonlinear analysis, ordinary and partial differential equations, fuzzy differential equations, mathematical modelling, epidemiology and financial mathematics. Her work has explored the existence of solutions to nonlinear differential equations, optimal control models and applications of mathematics to public health and finance.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=WALO OMANA REBECCA
 |url=https://www.unikin.ac.cd/oipr/OIPR/chercheurs/963/WALO-OMANA-REBECCA
 |website=University of Kinshasa
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==

* Omana, Rebecca; Ramadhani, Issa (2010). "A critical point theorem for noncontinuous functionals". ''International Journal of Functional Analysis, Operator Theory and Applications''.
* Omana, Rebecca (2008). "Periodic solution of nonlinear fuzzy differential equations". ''Advances in Fuzzy Sets and Systems''.
* Mawhin, Jean; Omana, Rebecca (1992). "A priori bounds and existence of positive solutions for some singular superlinear boundary value problems". ''Funkcialaj Ekvacioj''.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Rebecca Walo Omana – Publications
 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rebecca-Walo-Omana
 |website=ResearchGate
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>


== Mentorship ==

Throughout her academic career, Omana has supervised doctoral students in mathematics and has encouraged the participation of women in advanced mathematical research in the Democratic Republic of the Congo through postgraduate training and academic mentoring.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=WALO OMANA REBECCA
 |url=https://www.unikin.ac.cd/oipr/OIPR/chercheurs/963/WALO-OMANA-REBECCA
 |website=University of Kinshasa
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>


== Honours ==

In 2024, the University of Kinshasa recognised Omana as Professor Emerita, acknowledging her long-standing contributions to mathematics teaching, research and higher education in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Première dame mathématicienne à accéder à l'éméritat en RDC
 |url=https://www.unikin.ac.cd/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Hebdo-74-du-SGR-2024.pdf
 |website=University of Kinshasa
 |access-date=14 July 2026
}}</ref>
